title: A Tutorial on Quantum Amplitude Embedding with Data Re-Uploading
abstract: Amplitude embedding lets a variational quantum model read many classical features with few qubits, but the model output is then only a quadratic form in the normalized input. Data re-uploading, which encodes the input repeatedly between trainable blocks, can be used to enrich such a model. Because every additional upload of an amplitude embedding repeats a costly state preparation, the gain that an upload buys has to be known before the gates are spent. This tutorial thus addresses the problem of explaining what data re-uploading adds to an amplitude-embedded model and how large the gain is. We express sequential re-uploading and parallel re-uploading with two copies in one notation and show that each upload raises the reachable polynomial order by two. Under one trainable circuit family and one budget of trainable parameters, simulation results show that re-uploading raises the test coefficient of determination from 0.689 to between 0.883 and 0.975 on targets of order four and from 0.337 to between 0.642 and 0.783 on targets of order six, on all ten seeds. On a quadratic target and on handwritten digits, one upload remains the best choice, and every additional upload lowers the gate error that the classifier tolerates. These results help designers match the number of uploads to the polynomial order of the task at hand.
summary: This tutorial analyzes how repeatedly re-uploading classical data into a quantum amplitude embedding model increases its expressive power by raising the reachable polynomial order. The authors demonstrate that while more uploads increase capacity, this benefit is not always optimal, showing that for many tasks, one upload is sufficient, and excessive uploads can degrade performance due to accumulated gate errors.
main_problem: The paper aims to explain the functional gain provided by data re-uploading in amplitude-embedded variational quantum models and to quantify this performance improvement.
main_result: Re-uploading enriches the model by raising the reachable polynomial order by two per upload, but for tasks like quadratic classification, one upload is optimal, as further uploads degrade performance and increase gate error.
method: The authors analyze sequential and parallel re-uploading schemes, deriving the resulting polynomial order and comparing performance metrics like the test coefficient of determination across different upload counts.
model_or_system: The model utilizes amplitude embedding within variational quantum circuits, where the input data is encoded into the amplitudes of qubits. Re-uploading involves repeatedly encoding the input state between trainable quantum blocks.
key_observables: Test coefficient of determination ($R^2$), classifier fidelity, and the polynomial order of the target function.
important_parameters: The number of uploads ($L$ or $k$), the polynomial order of the target (e.g., order four or six), and the two-qubit gate error rate ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a fixed budget of trainable parameters and that the gain must be known before spending costly state preparation gates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model structure with one upload and show comparisons between encoding methods. One figure details re-uploading schemes (sequential vs. parallel), and another tracks performance degradation versus gate error.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces amplitude embedding and the problem of re-uploading. It then provides a theoretical analysis comparing sequential and parallel re-uploading schemes regarding the polynomial order. Finally, it presents simulation results on synthetic targets and handwritten digits to quantify the performance gain and error tolerance.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum machine learning, the analysis of circuit depth, resource scaling, and error accumulation due to repeated state preparation is highly relevant to designing fault-tolerant quantum algorithms and understanding the limits of variational quantum circuits.
